title: Apple supplier weak guidance sends peers into negative territory AAPL;LITE;IIVI;TSM - The Fly
text:
On The Fly: What to watch in Coca-Cola earnings report » Coca-Cola (KO) is… 
Coca-Cola (KO) is scheduled to report results of its fiscal first quarter before the market open on Tuesday, April 24, with a conference call scheduled for 9:00 am ET. What to watch for: 1. GUIDANCE: When Coca-Cola reported fourth quarter earnings on February 16, the company said it saw fiscal year 2018 earnings per share up 8%-10%, with organic revenue growth of approximately 4%, and 8%-9% growth in comparable currency neutral operating income. Management added that it would continue to see structural headwinds in 2018, and that the majority of 2018 earnings growth would be in the second half of the year. 2. DIET COKE RELAUNCH: After announcing a re-launch of Diet Coke with a new look in January, with "sleek" 12 ounce cans, and four new flavors -- Diet Coke Ginger Lime, Diet Coke Feisty Cherry, Diet Coke Zesty Blood Orange and Diet Coke Twisted Mango -- investors will be interested in seeing early results from the new flavors, especially with some analysts expressing skepticism that any drinks with artificial sweeteners can appeal to modern health conscious consumers. 3. TAX FIGHT WITH IRS: Earlier in April, Coca-Cola sued the Internal Revenue Service over a $3.3B bill for back taxes arguing the agency previously approved the company's method for setting transfer prices for foreign affiliates in a 1966 agreement but later withdrew the approval and issued the bill, according to a Reuters report, citing the case. The trial, which is expected to end in April, is being closely watched by tax experts amid elevated tension between tax authorities and multinational corporations over transfer pricing, which is under more scrutiny than ever before by tax agencies worldwide due to tighter global standards. 4: GOLDMAN RATINGS SHAKE-UP: On April 17, Goldman Sachs analyst Judy Hong upgraded Coca-Cola to Neutral while reducing her price target for the shares to $46 from $47. The analyst coupled the upgrade with a downgrade of PepsiCo (PEP) to Sell. For Coca-Cola, the analyst sees an improving organic sales growth outlook, "cleaner base" post-refranchising, and better visibility on its margin and earnings targets. She called the company "one of the rare" over 4% organic growth mega-cap stories in Americas Beverages. Hong said she believes PepsiCo's organic growth underperformance relative to Coca-Cola could widen. Further, Coca-Cola's current price-to-earnings premium versus PepsiCo of 10% could widen to 15%, the analyst contended. KO
